transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate you taking the time. 

Um... I guess I'm here because... well, I've been a little bit on edge lately? Actually, it's—it's more than that, and it's really embarrassing to admit. I keep sort of... blowing up at people over absolutely nothing. I work in retail, and the other day I actually yelled at one of my employees just for putting some stock on the wrong shelf. 

I felt so terrible about it. I had to go in the back because I was just shaking afterward. I just want you to know, that is really not how I usually treat people. I pride myself on being a good, supportive manager, so acting like that is just... it's very out of character for me. I'm just not myself right now. I hope it's okay that I came in for this?
Have you been feeling anxious or nervous more often than usual lately?

Um... anxious? I guess... I wouldn't necessarily use the word anxious. I really don't want to sound dramatic or, you know, make a big deal out of nothing. It's mostly just... a lot of stress, I think? 

I mean, I know everyone deals with stress, and I usually handle my responsibilities really well. I definitely don't want you to think I can't handle my job. It's just... lately, I do feel a little more wound up than normal, I suppose. Just that on-edge feeling I mentioned. Is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm answering your questions right.
Do you find yourself having repetitive thoughts that are difficult to stop?

Repetitive thoughts? Um... no, I don't think so. Not really. I mean, I think about work a lot, making sure the schedule is right and the floor looks good, but that's just being responsible, right? I try to stay really organized. 

I wouldn't say I have thoughts that I can't stop. I can usually distract myself if I need to. I really try not to let my mind run away with things, because I know how important it is to stay positive and focused. Does that make sense? I just... I don't want to give you the wrong impression and make it sound like I'm obsessing over things, because I'm really not.
Have you been avoiding certain situations or activities lately?

Um... avoiding things? Well... I guess maybe a little bit? But it's just because I've been so busy with work, really. 

Although... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest—and I feel so silly even saying this out loud—I haven't really been going back to my house very much. I've been staying with a friend. And... well, I haven't been able to look at the mortgage folder on the counter. Or even the little herb garden I have on the patio. 

It sounds completely ridiculous, I know. I should just be able to go home and deal with things like a normal person. But lately, anything that reminds me of... of that day... it just makes my chest feel so tight, and I just can't seem to force myself to go near any of it. I'm really trying to push past it, I promise. I know it's not a healthy way to cope. Is it okay that I'm struggling with that a little bit? I don't want you to think I'm just running away from my problems.
Do you feel like you're doing anything over and over to try and calm yourself or make yourself feel better?

Um... over and over? No, I don't think so. I definitely don't do anything strange or out of the ordinary, I promise. 

I try to just... take a few deep breaths if I'm feeling too tense, like people say you're supposed to do. Sometimes at work I'll maybe reorganize a clothing rack or tidy up a display just to keep my hands busy for a second, but that's just being productive, right? I definitely don't have any weird habits or anything I'm relying on like that. I really want to make sure I'm coping the right way, so... I hope I'm doing okay there. Is that the right kind of answer?
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

Sad? Um... no, not really. I mean, I definitely wouldn't say I'm depressed or anything like that. I try really hard to keep a smile on my face, especially at work. You have to be upbeat for the customers, you know? 

I guess... well, maybe I've been a little more tired than usual? And sometimes I just feel sort of... flat, I guess. Like things that usually make me happy just don't have the same spark right now. But I'm sure that's just because I haven't been sleeping great and I'm stressed, right? Everyone gets a little down when they're stressed. 

I really try to focus on the positive things and count my blessings. I definitely don't want to sit around feeling sorry for myself. I'm doing my best to stay cheerful, I really am. I hope that's what you're looking for... I just want to make sure I'm handling this the right way.
Do you feel compelled to perform specific rituals or behaviors to reduce your anxiety?

Rituals? Um... no, definitely not. I think... maybe that's kind of like what you were just asking a minute ago, right? About doing things over and over? 

I promise I don't have anything like that going on. I don't feel forced to do any specific little routines or anything. Just, you know, keeping my hands busy straightening up the store like I mentioned, but that's just being a good employee. I definitely don't have any strange behaviors or anything I'm hiding from you, I swear. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have anything like that to report? I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure all this out, so... I hope I'm being helpful.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'that day' that's been making it hard for you to go home?

Um... well, it's just... I guess I've been staying away from the house a lot lately. I know that probably sounds silly, a grown woman avoiding her own home, but... I just can't seem to make myself go back there right now. 

It's not just the house, either. It's... well, I haven't even looked at the mortgage folder, and I've completely ignored my little patio herb garden, which I usually love tending to. I know I should be keeping up with my responsibilities, I really do. It's just that... whenever I get near anything that reminds me of what happened, my chest gets so tight I can hardly breathe, and I just... I can't do it. 

I know I need to get over it and go home, and I promise I'm trying to work up the courage. I'm not trying to be difficult or run away from my problems, I swear. Is it... is it normal to feel this way? I just want to make sure I'm not completely failing at handling this.
Can you tell me what happened on the day that's been making it hard for you to go home?

Um... well, it was about two weeks ago. We had just started working on the house—it was our first weekend really getting into it. And... um... there was a fire. In the kitchen. 

I know it probably sounds like I'm overreacting, staying away for two whole weeks just because of a kitchen fire. I mean, the fire department came and put it out, and nobody was hurt, so I really should just be grateful and move on, right? I'm sure other people bounce back from this sort of thing much faster. 

I just... I haven't been able to shake it since that day. I'm really trying, though. I promise I'm not just giving up. I hope you don't think I'm being completely ridiculous about this... is it okay that it's taking me a little time to get over it?
Do you think the fire in your kitchen was the main reason you've been avoiding your home?

Um... yes, definitely. It's the fire. I mean, I know I already mentioned staying away from the house, and the mortgage folder... even my patio herbs. I just... I can't go near any of it. 

I know it sounds so weak, and I really don't want you to think I'm just running away from my problems. But any little thing tied to that day... my chest just gets so tight, and I freeze up. I just can't make myself go near any of it right now. 

I'm really trying to be brave about it, I promise. I know I should be handling this better. Is it... does that make sense, that the fire would make me avoid all those other things too? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Are there any other places or situations, besides your home, that you've been avoiding since the fire?

Um... no, not really. It's just the house and... and the things connected to it, like I mentioned. 

I mean, I'm still going to work at the store, and I can go to the grocery store and run my errands just fine. I don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart or anything. I'm really trying to keep the rest of my life as normal as possible. 

I guess I just... I haven't noticed anywhere else bothering me like the house does. I'm doing my best to stay functional everywhere else, I swear. Is that... is that a good sign? That it's mostly just the house I'm having trouble with?
Have you been experiencing any memories or images of the fire that come into your mind without you wanting them to?

Um... yeah. Yes, I have. I really wish I could say no, because I know I should be moving past it by now, but... the fire just keeps jumping into my head out of nowhere. 

It's... it's so stupid, but I'll just be doing something completely normal, like picking up a pan at the store to stock it, or opening a spreadsheet at work, and suddenly... suddenly I'm right back there. I can smell the smoke, and I see the kitchen filling up with it, and it happens before I can even stop myself. 

I'm so sorry, I know I shouldn't be letting it interrupt my day like that. I really try to push it away as soon as it happens, I promise. I don't want to be one of those people who just dwells on things. Does... does that happen to other people too? The memories just popping up like that? I hope you don't think I'm just letting my imagination run wild.
Have you been having any nightmares about the fire?

Um... no, actually. No nightmares. I mean, I've been sleeping okay, I think. 

I really try to clear my head before bed, you know? I don't want to bring all that stress into my sleep. So, no, I haven't been waking up terrified or anything like that. I'm really trying to make sure I get good rest so I can keep functioning at work. 

I guess that's a positive thing, right? That at least my sleep isn't being ruined by it? I really hope that shows I'm handling things somewhat well... at least at night.
Have you been avoiding people who were with you during the fire?

Um... no, definitely not. I mean, my husband was there with me, and I would never shut him out. I'm really trying to make sure I'm still being a good partner, you know? 

I haven't been avoiding anyone at all. I know it's important to keep your support system close, so I've been making a real effort to talk to everyone just like normal. I don't want my issues to become a burden on the people I care about, so I'm doing my best to be there for them, too. 

That's... that's the right way to handle it, isn't it? I just really don't want to make things harder for anyone else.
Do you find yourself being constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try to just go about my day normally. 

I know some people get really paranoid after something bad happens, but I'm really trying not to be like that. I don't want to be jumping at shadows or making my husband feel like he has to walk on eggshells around me. I just... I try to stay focused on what I'm doing, like at the store or at home. 

I mean, maybe I double-check the stove a little more carefully now, but that's just being responsible, right? I'm not, like, constantly looking over my shoulder or anything. I really want to just be sensible about it. Does that sound okay? I just don't want to overreact.
How did you feel immediately after the fire happened?

Um... right after? I think... I think I was okay, mostly. 

I mean, obviously it was a shock, but I really tried to just hold it together. I didn't want to be one of those people who completely falls apart and makes a scene, you know? My husband was there, and I just wanted to make sure he was alright, so I stayed pretty calm. 

I just stood out of the way and tried to be helpful if the firemen needed anything. I wasn't hysterical or crying uncontrollably or anything like that. I figured the best thing to do was just... stay quiet and let the professionals do their job. 

That's the best way to handle an emergency, isn't it? Just staying calm so you aren't a burden to the first responders? I really tried my best to be good about it and not cause any extra trouble.
Have you felt detached from yourself or your surroundings since the fire?

Um... no, not really detached. I mean, I'm still going to work and getting everything done. 

I guess... well, sometimes when I'm walking through the store at work, it feels a little strange. Like... like I'm sort of watching myself from a few feet away? And the aisles and the customers are there, but they don't seem entirely real. Like I'm just kind of moving through it all on automatic. 

But I'm still doing my job! I'm still helping people and smiling. I think it's just because I'm a little tired, you know? It's perfectly normal to space out a bit when you're working retail, right? I just don't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality or anything. I'm still functioning perfectly fine. That's just a normal reaction to being busy, isn't it?
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I still like doing things. 

My husband and I usually have a movie night on Fridays, and we still do that. I guess... maybe I haven't been quite as talkative during the movies lately, or maybe I don't always pay as close attention to the plot as I used to. But I still sit there with him, and I make the popcorn just like always. 

I just... I think it's normal to have an off week or two where you just want to sit quietly, right? I don't want him to think I'm ruining our routine or being a downer. I'm really trying to keep things pleasant at home. It's perfectly fine to just want a little quiet time, isn't it? I'm still participating, so that means I haven't lost interest, right?
Have you found that you don't enjoy activities as much as you used to since the fire happened?

Um... no, not really. I think I still enjoy things just fine. 

I mean, like I said about movie night, I'm still doing all the things I usually do. I guess maybe I haven't been quite as... enthusiastic about going out or doing my hobbies. Like, I used to really love working in the garden on the weekends, and I haven't done much of that lately. But it's been so hot out, you know? It makes sense to just want to stay inside where the AC is. 

I'm still doing my best to be involved and keep a smile on my face, though. I don't want anyone to think I'm depressed or letting this whole thing get the better of me. I'm just taking it a little easy, which is the smart thing to do after something stressful, right? You'd agree that it's okay to just rest a bit more than usual, wouldn't you?

doctor.question: Have you been having any nightmares about the fire?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about nightmares related to the trauma, which is a specific intrusive symptom (typically coded separately as distressing dreams/nightmares in PTSD/ASD criteria). My symptom profile includes 'Intrusive_Symptoms' (S069) for intrusive distressing memories, but does not explicitly mention nightmares or sleep disturbances.

patient.answer:
Um... no, actually. No nightmares. I mean, I've been sleeping okay, I think. 

I really try to clear my head before bed, you know? I don't want to bring all that stress into my sleep. So, no, I haven't been waking up terrified or anything like that. I'm really trying to make sure I get good rest so I can keep functioning at work. 

I guess that's a positive thing, right? That at least my sleep isn't being ruined by it? I really hope that shows I'm handling things somewhat well... at least at night.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of avoidance of people or places due to fear of triggering memories of the fire
doctor.question: Have you been avoiding people who were with you during the fire?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient has been avoiding people who were with her during the fire, which falls under Trauma Avoidance. The patient's profile for Trauma Avoidance (S070) mentions avoiding the house, mortgage folder, and herbs on the patio, but does not mention avoiding people. Therefore, the profile does not cover this specific question.

patient.answer:
Um... no, definitely not. I mean, my husband was there with me, and I would never shut him out. I'm really trying to make sure I'm still being a good partner, you know? 

I haven't been avoiding anyone at all. I know it's important to keep your support system close, so I've been making a real effort to talk to everyone just like normal. I don't want my issues to become a burden on the people I care about, so I'm doing my best to be there for them, too. 

That's... that's the right way to handle it, isn't it? I just really don't want to make things harder for anyone else.

doctor.question: Do you find yourself being constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about hypervigilance (being constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats), which is not included in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Um... no, not really. I mean, I try to just go about my day normally. 

I know some people get really paranoid after something bad happens, but I'm really trying not to be like that. I don't want to be jumping at shadows or making my husband feel like he has to walk on eggshells around me. I just... I try to stay focused on what I'm doing, like at the store or at home. 

I mean, maybe I double-check the stove a little more carefully now, but that's just being responsible, right? I'm not, like, constantly looking over my shoulder or anything. I really want to just be sensible about it. Does that sound okay? I just don't want to overreact.

doctor.intent: Determine the patient's emotional response to the fire
doctor.question: How did you feel immediately after the fire happened?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the patient's immediate feelings or emotional state right after the traumatic event (the fire). The symptom profile does not contain a specific symptom related to the immediate emotional reaction or acute distress right after the event.

patient.answer:
Um... right after? I think... I think I was okay, mostly. 

I mean, obviously it was a shock, but I really tried to just hold it together. I didn't want to be one of those people who completely falls apart and makes a scene, you know? My husband was there, and I just wanted to make sure he was alright, so I stayed pretty calm. 

I just stood out of the way and tried to be helpful if the firemen needed anything. I wasn't hysterical or crying uncontrollably or anything like that. I figured the best thing to do was just... stay quiet and let the professionals do their job. 

That's the best way to handle an emergency, isn't it? Just staying calm so you aren't a burden to the first responders? I really tried my best to be good about it and not cause any extra trouble.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of dissociative symptoms
doctor.question: Have you felt detached from yourself or your surroundings since the fire?

target_item.name: Depersonalization_Derealization
target_item.manifestation: Sometimes when I’m walking through the store it feels like I’m watching myself from a few feet away, like the aisles and customers are there but not quite real and I’m just moving through them on automatic.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling detached from oneself or one's surroundings, which directly corresponds to the symptom of Depersonalization_Derealization.

patient.answer:
Um... no, not really detached. I mean, I'm still going to work and getting everything done. 

I guess... well, sometimes when I'm walking through the store at work, it feels a little strange. Like... like I'm sort of watching myself from a few feet away? And the aisles and the customers are there, but they don't seem entirely real. Like I'm just kind of moving through it all on automatic. 

But I'm still doing my job! I'm still helping people and smiling. I think it's just because I'm a little tired, you know? It's perfectly normal to space out a bit when you're working retail, right? I just don't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality or anything. I'm still functioning perfectly fine. That's just a normal reaction to being busy, isn't it?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has a loss of interest in activities they once enjoyed
doctor.question: Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities (anhedonia), which is not covered by any of the symptoms in my profile.

patient.answer:
Um... no, not really. I mean, I still like doing things. 

My husband and I usually have a movie night on Fridays, and we still do that. I guess... maybe I haven't been quite as talkative during the movies lately, or maybe I don't always pay as close attention to the plot as I used to. But I still sit there with him, and I make the popcorn just like always. 

I just... I think it's normal to have an off week or two where you just want to sit quietly, right? I don't want him to think I'm ruining our routine or being a downer. I'm really trying to keep things pleasant at home. It's perfectly fine to just want a little quiet time, isn't it? I'm still participating, so that means I haven't lost interest, right?

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of marked diminished interest in activities
doctor.question: Have you found that you don't enjoy activities as much as you used to since the fire happened?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about anhedonia (loss of enjoyment in activities), which is not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Um... no, not really. I think I still enjoy things just fine. 

I mean, like I said about movie night, I'm still doing all the things I usually do. I guess maybe I haven't been quite as... enthusiastic about going out or doing my hobbies. Like, I used to really love working in the garden on the weekends, and I haven't done much of that lately. But it's been so hot out, you know? It makes sense to just want to stay inside where the AC is. 

I'm still doing my best to be involved and keep a smile on my face, though. I don't want anyone to think I'm depressed or letting this whole thing get the better of me. I'm just taking it a little easy, which is the smart thing to do after something stressful, right? You'd agree that it's okay to just rest a bit more than usual, wouldn't you?
